evidence.rule: At 13:30 CT (30 min before 14:00 CT, the paper's FX close; Euro FX hours 07:20-14:00), long if r_ROD = P(13:30)/P(prior 14:00 close) - 1 > 0, short if < 0; exit 14:00 CT
evidence.conversion: 0.85%/yr (1/N portfolio of 8 currency futures, Table 6 Panel D) / 252 trading days = 0.337 bp per day; bp->ticks at EUR/USD 1.11 (2019-2024 mean of ECB annual reference-rate averages, pages/6E/ecb_exr_usd_eur_annual_2010_2024.csv): 1 tick (0.00005) = 0.4505 bp

evidence.decay_evidence: Subsample Table 5 Panel B 2000-2020: currency beta_ROD 0.33 (t 1.45), insignificant (1974-1999: 1.31, t 6.48). evidence.effect: Post-London-fix U.S. dollar depreciation (EUR appreciates after the 16:00 London fix)
evidence.rule: Long EUR/USD from the London fix (11:00 ET = 10:00 CT) to 17:00 ET (16:00 CT), every day
evidence.hold: 6 h (10:00-16:00 CT); inside the 6E day session up to F 15:08 CT
evidence.conversion: Table I EUR post-L 2.73 bp per day; bp->ticks at EUR/USD 1.11 (2019-2024 mean of ECB annual reference-rate averages, pages/6E/ecb_exr_usd_eur_annual_2010_2024.csv): 1 tick (0.00005) = 0.4505 bp
evidence.decay_evidence: Dollar portfolio post-L by subsample (Table II): 2.80 (99-03), 2.29 (04-09), 1.43 (10-13, t 1.80), 0.86 (14-19, t 1.62). CME futures dollar portfolio 2006-2019 (Table III): 0.64 bp (t 2.20). Liquidity-demander returns after costs negative (Table X, AUD and GBP, post-L -2.83 and -0.44 bp). No post-2019 or post-publication evidence found.
evidence.source: Krohn, Mueller, Whelan (2024), Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns Around the Clock, Journal of Finance 79(1) 541-578 (author accepted manuscript, Jan 2023)
evidence.quote: 'After the London fix, the pattern is again quite striking: with the exception of the yen, all currencies appreciate strongly (i.e., between 1.5 bps for the Canadian dollar and 2.7 bps for the euro) during the period between the London fix and the close of markets in the U.S.' Table I: 'EUR -1.80 2.34 -3.53 0.63 2.73 0.36 / (-8.84) (9.29) (-7.25) (1.36) (6.78) (0.43)'. Table II: '14-19 -0.63 0.82 -1.25 -0.60 0.86 -0.80'. Table III: 'CME Futures -1.46 1.80 -1.64 0.11 0.64 -0.56 / (-8.94) (9.37) (-4.76) (0.30) (2.20) (-0.90)'. 'for the trader (or liquidity demander), reversal returns turn negative once transaction costs are taken into account.'
evidence.quote_location: text p.10; Table I p.31; Table II p.32; Table III p.33; Table X discussion p.27, Table X p.40; window definitions ('post-L,' 11:00 to 17:00 ET) p.8

evidence.decay_evidence: Turning point moved by 15 min in July 2016 (Panel C: 08:15-08:30 ET -0.07, t -0.44). K3-ecbfix's T_E = 14:15 Berlin is the pre-2016 turning point.
evidence.quote: Panel B: 'EUR -0.61 -0.89 0.96 / (-4.76) (-7.31) (7.53)'; Panel C: 'EUR -1.33 1.04 -0.07 / (-6.08) (5.93) (-0.44)'. evidence.effect: End-of-month WMR fix reversal (contrarian after the 4 pm fix)
evidence.rule: On the last trading day of the month, at 16:00 London take a long (short) position if the fix is below (above) the price h minutes earlier; hold h = 1, 5, 15 min
evidence.conversion: EUR/USD h=15: 3.965 (annual percent), Sharpe 1.881, net of one half the average EBS spread at exit. The annualization convention for a once-a-month trade is not stated, so a per-trade bp figure is not derivable without an assumption (x252 gives 1.57 bp, x12 gives 33 bp).
evidence.sample: 21 currency pairs, 2004-2013, Gain Capital 1-s data and EBS; fix window 1 min (pre-2015 methodology)
evidence.decay_evidence: Author reports pre-2010 estimates similar and post-2010 out-of-sample average 3.25% across the best pre-2010 pairs. Sample ends before the 2015-02-15 widening of the fix window to 5 min. Basis of K3-ldnrev (on 6E).
evidence.source: Evans (2018), Forex trading and the WMR Fix, J. Banking & Finance 87, 233-247 (MPRA 81583, Sept 2017 forthcoming version)
evidence.quote: 'A: EUR/USD 3.965 0.486 0.068 1.881 0.222 0.042 1.791 1.780 1.732'; notes: 'Columns (i) - (iii) report the average return (in annual percent) from a trading strategy of holding a long (short) position for horizon h = {1, 5, 15} minutes following the end-of-month Fix if the Fix is below (above) the price level h minutes earlier.' 'Returns are inclusive of trading costs, computed to be zero at the Fix and one half the average bid-ask spread when the position is closed.' 'I also calculated the post-2010 returns on the strategy for each currency pair that had the highest Sharpe Ratio in the pre-2010 data. This produced an average return across the currencies of 3.25 percent.'

evidence.effect: Month-end equity-hedge rebalancing before the 4 pm fix (Melvin and Prins)
evidence.rule: Last day of month: currency return 15:00-16:00 London regressed on the country's month-to-date equity return (first to second-last day of month, close to close), both cross-sectionally demeaned over 10 currencies (USD included): coefficient -0.0142
evidence.conversion: per 1% of relative month-to-date equity return: 0.0142 x 100 bp = 1.42 bp ('10% equity appreciation leads to 14 basis points'); bp->ticks at EUR/USD 1.11 (2019-2024 mean of ECB annual reference-rate averages, pages/6E/ecb_exr_usd_eur_annual_2010_2024.csv): 1 tick (0.00005) = 0.4505 bp
evidence.sample: 10 currencies, 5-min TWAPs from EBS/Reuters, 2004-04-28..2012-12-31; Datastream total-market equity indices
evidence.decay_evidence: None found after 2012. The fix window widened from 1 to 5 min on 2015-02-15 (BIS, Debelle 2015). Published JFM 22 (2015) 50-72 version not retrieved (paywalled); figures here are from the 2013 ECB-workshop draft.
evidence.source: Melvin, Prins (2015), Equity hedging and exchange rates at the London 4 p.m. fix, J. Financial Markets 22, 50-72 (Nov 2013 working-paper draft hosted by the ECB)
evidence.quote: 'The results show that an equity market appreciation over the month predicts a statistically significant depreciation in the currency in the hour leading up to the end of month fix. The implied magnitude is that a 10% equity appreciation leads to 14 basis points of currency depreciation.' 'where r_i,T^FX is the currency return from 15:00 to 16:00 London time on the last day of the month (a positive return reflects strengthening of the currency), and r_i,T-1^EQ is the equity return from the first to the second last day of the month (market close to market close).' 'At each period, we subtract the cross-section mean return of currencies against the USD.'

evidence.effect: FOMC-day currency drift and reversal (foreign currencies appreciate before and at the announcement, reverse 12-24 h later)
evidence.rule: Long foreign currency vs USD in the 12-hour window before a scheduled FOMC statement (02:15-14:15 EST), reverse after +12 h
evidence.hold: 12-hour half-day windows (overlaps the 6E day session only partly)
evidence.conversion: Dollar factor -12:0hr 23.407 (% per annum), 0:12hr 13.751, 12:24hr -47.521; the annualization of a 12-hour window return is not stated (x504 half-days gives 4.6 bp per pre-FOMC window, x252 gives 9.3 bp). EUR-specific numbers are in figures only.
evidence.decay_evidence: Published version (Lee and Wang, RAPS 15(3-4) 2025, 247-287) not retrieved; abstract per search engine reports the reversal cancels about 65% of the pre-announcement drift [secondary-only]. Borisenko and Pozdeev find the related Karnaukh dollar pre-FOMC drift averages to zero across specifications [secondary-only, not fetched]. 6E's D8 list already includes FOMC (g13-g15).
evidence.source: Wang (2018), Essays on currency markets, PhD dissertation, Georgia Institute of Technology, ch.1 (published as Lee and Wang 2025, Review of Asset Pricing Studies)
evidence.quote: 'Dollar factor 0.085 23.115 23.407 13.751 -47.521' (Panel A, Excess return (% per annum), columns Overall, -24:-12hr, -12:0hr, 0:12hr, 12:24hr). 'because scheduled FOMC announcements occur at 14:15 EST, non-overlapping half-day windows are partitioned at 02:15 and 14:15 EST.'
evidence.quote_location: Table 1.1 Panel A p.38; text p.10

evidence.effect: ECB communication outside meeting days: no EUR/USD drift (null)
evidence.rule: Event study of 1,868 coded ECB statements; cumulative abnormal returns over 20 minutes
evidence.conversion: null: CARs within about +-2 bp by t = +20 min; no rule
evidence.source: Fanta (2025), ECB monetary policy communication: an event study on intraday returns and volatility in the EUR/USD FX market, IES Working Paper 23/2025 (Czech J. Economics and Finance 76(2), 2026)
evidence.quote: 'Across the full sample and every split, price responses are small and short-lived. Cumulative abnormal returns remain within a few basis points by t=+20, and scattered significant minutes are not sequential.' 'We find no reliably detectable intraday drift under conservative'
evidence.quote_location: abstract; introduction p.3 (line 134 of the text extraction)

proposed_features.name: p6e_mehedge_nq
proposed_features.source: Melvin and Prins (2015, JFM 22:50-72), 2013 ECB-workshop draft, pp.13-14 (E6)
proposed_features.quote: 'an equity market appreciation over the month predicts a statistically significant depreciation in the currency in the hour leading up to the end of month fix. The implied magnitude is that a 10% equity appreciation leads to 14 basis points of currency depreciation.' / 'At each period, we subtract the cross-section mean return of currencies against the USD.'
proposed_features.formula: On trade date d = ME(m), the last FX trade date of calendar month m (FX group calendar; hist2010/fx.json before 2019-05, data/calendars/fx.py after), at t1 = 07:50 CT: value = ln( C_NQ(e_prev) / C_NQ(e_base) ), where C_NQ(x) is the close of NQ's last 1-min bar ending at or before 15:00 CT (equity group C) on equity trade date x, e_prev = the last equity trade date strictly before d's calendar date, e_base = the last equity trade date of month m-1. On every other date or decision time: 0 and flag 0. Sign: positive value predicts 6E up (USD depreciation) in the 09:00-10:00 CT pre-fix hour, because in the paper's demeaned panel EUR/USD's predicted return is +0.0142 x (r_US_eq - r_EU_eq) and only the US leg is among the 17 roots. Differences from the paper: NQ stands in for the US total-market index; the euro-area equity leg is missing (no free EURO STOXX 50 history, and it is not one of the 17 roots); the base is the previous month's last close, as in K3-mehedge, while the paper says 'from the first to the second last day of the month'.
calendars: FX group calendar (month ends): hist2010/fx.json 2010-06-01..2019-05-31, data/calendars/fx.py 2019-05-01..2026-06-19
equity group calendar for NQ closes: hist2010/equity.json 2010-06-01..2019-05-31, data/calendars/equity.py
proposed_features.derivation: Expected figure and ratio are per 1% of relative month-to-date equity return (conditional slope, not an unconditional mean). 1.42 bp per 1% of relative (US minus euro-area) month-to-date equity return over the full 60-min pre-fix hour; the t1/h120 hold (07:50-09:50 CT) overlaps 50 of those 60 min in standard weeks (pro rata 1.18 bp) and none of them in C9 mismatch weeks (T_L 11:00 CT). 1.18 bp / 0.4505 bp per tick = 2.63 ticks per 1% of relative return. 1.5 x D8 = 3.458 ticks (1.56 bp) needs a relative return of at least 1.32%. NQ alone measures the relative return only partly (the euro-area leg is missing), so the realized slope on the NQ-only value is smaller than 0.0142 by an unknown factor. The unconditional mean per trade is not derivable from the paper. About 12 events a year (about 106 in the backward window, 58 in the search window).

proposed_features.name: p6e_post_ldnfix
proposed_features.source: Krohn, Mueller and Whelan (2024, JF 79(1) 541-578), Table I and p.10 (E2)
proposed_features.quote: 'After the London fix, the pattern is again quite striking: with the exception of the yen, all currencies appreciate strongly (i.e., between 1.5 bps for the Canadian dollar and 2.7 bps for the euro) during the period between the London fix and the close of markets in the U.S.'
proposed_features.formula: On every 6E row: T_L(d) = 16:00 Europe/London on calendar date d converted to CT with zoneinfo (10:00 CT, 11:00 CT in C9 mismatch weeks; same rule as k3/_clocks.py, extended to 2010-2019). Value at decision time t = minutes elapsed since T_L(d) if t >= T_L(d), applicability flag 1; else 0 and flag 0. Sign: positive applicability predicts 6E up to F (USD depreciates from the London fix to 17:00 ET).
calendars: T_L by rule (zoneinfo Europe/London and America/Chicago); FX group calendar both windows
proposed_features.derivation: Expected figure uses the latest published subsample (dollar portfolio 2014-2019, the closest to the search window). Full sample 1999-2019: EUR post-L 2.73 bp over 10:00-16:00 CT; t2 to F (10:20-15:08 CT, 4.8 of 6 h, pro rata) 2.18 bp = 4.85 ticks, ratio 2.10 to D8. Latest published subsample (dollar portfolio 2014-2019) 0.86 bp, pro rata 0.69 bp = 1.53 ticks, ratio 0.66. CME futures dollar portfolio 2006-2019 0.64 bp, pro rata 0.51 bp = 1.14 ticks, ratio 0.49. Fails 1.5x on the recent and on the futures-based evidence; the authors report liquidity-demander returns negative after costs. Overlap: away from mismatch weeks the value is a function of the decision time, which G11 together with the product identifier already carries.
